newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Small deterioration in NZ Oct trade balance trend.
newsitem.headline: Small deterioration in NZ Oct trade balance trend.

text.p: The trend in New Zealand's trade balance showed a small deterioration over September and October, following a period of steady improvement from February to August, Statistics New Zealand said on Monday.
Following the normal seasonal pattern, a NZ$195.6 million trade deficit was recorded for October.
The exports trend has declined over the last four months after rising from a low point in February. The trend in imports has also declined, but at a slower rate.

SNZ said the unadjusted value of exports in October was NZ$1.71 billion, up 2.9 percent on October 1995. The latest figure was a record high for exports in an October month and was largely a result of a 14.8 percent rise in dairy produce exports.
Unadjusted imports for October were valued at NZ$1.9 billion, up 0.2 percent. Imports of mechanical and electrical machinery, vehicles and mineral fuels continued to dominate import demand.

For the year ended October, unadjusted exports were down 0.6 percent on the previous year at NZ$20.95 billion. Dairy exports performed strongly, up 19.6 percent over the year to reach a value of $3.27 billion. Falls were recorded for other major export categories. Imports in the year rose 0.3 percent to $21.57 billion.

In the October quarter the trade deficit was NZ$844.9 million, which SNZ said was the largest deficit for an October quarter and the third largest quarterly deficit on record. However, if large irregular items, such as ships and aircraft, are excluded the quarterly deficit would have been $739 million.
Exports in the quarter were valued at NZ$4.92 billion, down 0.5 percent from the same quarter last year. Imports rose 1.3 percent to $5.76 billion.
